dataset.description: The purpose of the description was to explain how data will be collected and managed throughout the project to assess the impact of TiO2 quantum dots on the catalyst's mass activity and stability in acidic conditions. It outlines the types of data to be generated (e.g., synthesis, electrochemical testing, and characterization), the origin of this data (lab experiments), and the importance of the Data Management Plan (DMP) for ensuring that data is properly organized, stored, and shared according to scientific standards.

distribution.title: The purpose of data collection and generation in this project is to evaluate the effectiveness of conductive TiO2 quantum dots as a support material for enhancing the mass activity of IrO2 catalysts in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) under acidic conditions. This data will directly support the project's objectives of improving catalytic performance, stability, and efficiency. The data will be generated through experiments such as catalyst synthesis, electrochemical testing, and characterization techniques like SEM, XPS, and cyclic voltammetry. The origin of the data will stem from laboratory experiments conducted on synthesized and modified TiO2 quantum dots and IrO2 catalysts, followed by testing in electrochemical cells. The Data Management Plan ensures that all collected data is well-organized, stored securely, and shared in compliance with ethical and scientific standards.

dmp.description: The DMP will describe relevant aspects of making FAIR data: (i) Creation – experimental data will be created in open and lossless formats and organised using a file name convention. Types of data: the project will use data from different WPs/Tasks, specifically from multiple inputs laboratory experiments (e.g. sample photos, electron microscopy images, electrochemical measurements, and physical characterisation). (ii) Documentation and analysis – metadata and documentation will be created right after we go in accordance with Dublin Core standards. All datasets will be documented with metadata, codebooks will be shared, and variables will be described. Data will be shared under licences 'as open as possible, as closed as necessary', maximising the “protection before (open) dissemination”; (iii) Storing – data, documents, and document backups, as well as literature, will be stored in departmental “Cloud Storage”. A cloud that guarantees integrity by retaining data, maintaining security and protecting confidentiality and authenticity; (iv) Sharing and preservation: after the project, relevant data will be made open-access and preserved for a long time in a trusted Zenodo (OpenAire) repository under the CC BY-SA licence and applying its persistent IDs: DOIs and ORCIDs. Data will be cited from publications and reports. A first DMP (Deliverable D3.1) will be generated (Month 3) and updated (Months 12, 24, 36).
